title: ePA for all
summary:
Background: The electronic patient record (ePA) enables the collection and storage of medical data and allows for the rapid provision of relevant information such as diagnoses, treatments, and test results. In 2025, Germany transitioned the ePA system to an opt-out model.
Objectives: The ePA4all project aims to identify barriers, facilitators, and challenges related to the use of the ePA—on individual, structural, and application-related levels—in order to derive concrete recommendations for its successful implementation in routine healthcare practice.
Methods: Using a mixed-methods design, the study includes surveys and interviews with both users and non-users of the ePA, as well as stakeholders in healthcare provision, such as general practitioners and medical assistants, as well as personnel in emergency departments and physician assistants. In addition, routine data provided by gematik will be analyzed.
Impact on healthcare provision: The goal is to understand why people do or do not use the ePA in everyday healthcare settings. These insights will support the further development of the ePA and its successful integration into broad healthcare practice.
The project is funded for three years by the Innovation Fund of the Federal Joint Committee (G-BA) (funding reference: 01VSF24032).

interventions.name:
Module 1a: ePA Users
- 06/2025–05/2026: Interviews
- 11/2025–06/2026: Questionnaire survey

Module 1b: Non-users of the ePA (opted out of using the ePA)
- 06/2025–05/2026: Interviews
- 11/2025–06/2026: Questionnaire survey

Module 1c: Non-users of the ePA (Having an ePA but not using it)
- 06/2025–05/2026: Interviews
- 11/2025–06/2026: Questionnaire survey

Module 2: Routine data from gematik
- 11/2025–07/2027: descriptive and statistical association analyses of routine data (quarterly)

Module 3a: General practitioners and medical assistants
- 06/2025–05/2026: Interviews
- 11/2025–06/2026: Questionnaire survey

Module 3b: Emergency Department (emergency outpatient clinic, physician assistants)
- 06/2025–05/2026: Interviews
- 11/2025–06/2026: Questionnaire survey

Module 4: Development of target group-specific recommendations for action
- 03/2027–10/2027: Integration of findings, development of evidence-based recommendations, and consensus building through focus groups.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Module 1: Statutorily insured individuals
Module 3a: Currently working as a general practitioner or medical assistant
Module 3b: Currently working as medical staff in the emergency department or as a physician assistant
Exclusion criteria:
Module 1:
-Existing language barrier that impairs mutual comprehensible oral communication completely or only with the risk of a major loss of information.
-Severe cognitive impairment.
-Persons who do not give informed consent or withdraw it during the study.
Module 3:
-Stakeholders whose field of activity is not related to the use of the ePA
-Existing language barrier that impairs mutual comprehensible oral communication completely or only with the risk of a major loss of information
-Persons who do not give informed consent or withdraw it during the study
